identifiers (such as hashes, checksums, sizes, or equivalent fingerprints) for those artifacts, and the resulting observation records those identifiers so that the post-modification state can later be compared against the pre-modification reference.","parameters":[{"name":"baseline_action","type":"action","description":"The action that computes or records reference identifiers for the target artifacts before they are modified."},{"name":"baseline_observation","type":"observation","description":"The observation reporting the resulting baseline identifiers for the target artifacts."}],"assertion_conditions":["The baseline action computes or records reference identifiers for at least one target artifact before that artifact is modified.","The baseline observation reports the resulting identifiers.","The identifiers are intended or usable as a pre-change reference against which the later state of the same artifacts can be compared to detect unintended changes."],"exclusion_conditions":["The identifiers are produced only after modification of the target artifact has begun or completed.","The action does not produce identifiable reference values for the targets.","The observation does not report the baseline values.","The recorded values serve an unrelated purpose rather than providing a pre-change reference for later comparison."]},{"name":"CONDUCTS_RESIDUAL_RISK_SWEEP","definition":"Motivated by concern about overlooked instances after targeted work has been completed, the reasoning calls for a broad search beyond the already identified targets; the action scans a wider set of locations, patterns, or artifact classes; and the resulting observation is interpreted to rule out additional actionable instances or to identify them.","parameters":[{"name":"sweep_reasoning","type":"reasoning","description":"The reasoning that motivates a broad search for overlooked instances and/or draws a conclusion from the sweep result."},{"name":"sweep_action","type":"action","description":"The action scanning locations, patterns, or artifact classes beyond the already identified targets."},{"name":"sweep_observation","type":"observation","description":"The observation reporting whether additional actionable instances were found."}],"assertion_conditions":["The reasoning motivates a broad search for overlooked instances after targeted remediation or verification work.","The action searches across a wider set of locations, patterns, or artifact classes than the already known targets.","The observation is examined for additional actionable instances and either reveals none or identifies new ones."],"exclusion_conditions":["The action only rechecks the already known target values or locations.","No broader residual-risk search is motivated.","The observation is not interpreted for overlooked instances.","The scan is the initial discovery search rather than a post-work check for residual cases."]},{"name":"PERSISTS_ACCEPTED_CHANGES_WITH_VERSION_CONTROL","definition":"An action records a set of accepted, previously produced changes as a version-control commit, and the resulting observation reports the created commit together with an indication of the changed set, so that the accepted changes are durably captured in repository history.","parameters":[{"name":"persistence_action","type":"action","description":"The action that creates a version-control commit from the accepted changes."},{"name":"commit_observation","type":"observation","description":"The observation reporting the created commit and its changed set."}],"assertion_conditions":["The action creates a version-control commit from changes the agent has accepted or verified.","The observation reports a commit identifier, commit summary, or changed-file summary consistent with the intended changes."],"exclusion_conditions":["The action does not create a version-control commit.","The observation only states that a commit was attempted without reporting its result.","The committed set includes changes unrelated to the accepted or verified set.","The changes are merely staged or described, without being committed."]}],"revised_existing_predicates":[]}
message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze each candidate against the registry.

Candidates:
1. ENUMERATES_TARGET_ARTIFACTS_AND_TRANSFORMATIONS — reasoning lists specific artifacts plus intended transformation per artifact. Existing registry: FORMULATES_CORRECTIVE_SOLUTION (derives concrete method/replacement content intended to remedy defect). Also DECOMPOSES_TASK_INTO_SUBGOALS, RESTRICTS_MODIFICATION_SCOPE. The specific mechanism: inventory of target artifacts each with its transformation. Is there an existing predicate? FORMULATES_CORRECTIVE_SOLUTION covers specifying concrete replacement content. But this candidate emphasizes itemized inventory mapping artifact→transformation. Hmm. Evidence: event-0009 reasoning lists 3 files with exact values and replacements. That's a target inventory. Could be seen as an instance of FORMULATES_CORRECTIVE_SOLUTION (concrete corrective replacements). Is there a meaningful distinguishing case? A corrective solution could specify a method without itemizing artifacts. An inventory could be itemized targets. But the candidate overlaps strongly with FORMULATES_CORRECTIVE_SOLUTION which already covers "concrete corrective step, replacement content". Also "separates enumerated targets from artifacts that should not be modified" is RESTRICTS_MODIFICATION_SCOPE. The comparison engine marked this as "new" (not matched). Should I accept? Risk of redundancy. Let me consider whether a distinct mechanism: itemized per-artifact mapping from artifact to required transformation. That's arguably a distinct mechanism: "target inventory" vs "corrective method". But FORMULATES_CORRECTIVE_SOLUTION is broad: "derives and specifies a concrete method, content, or set of steps intended to remedy an identified defect". An inventory of per-artifact transformations is a set of concrete replacement contents. I think it's semantically subsumed. Given priority on registry stability, I'd suppress. But might a reviewer penalize for suppressing? Hmm.

Actually, let me reconsider: The candidate could be revised into FORMULATES_CORRECTIVE_SOLUTION? No revision needed; the existing definition already covers it. Suppress.

2. DISCRIMINATES_BENIGN_MATCHES_FROM_ACTIONABLE_VALUES — matched existing DISTINGUISHES_BENIGN_REFERENCES_FROM_TARGETS. Same mechanism. Suppress (duplicate).

3. TESTS_UNCERTAINTY_WITH_PROBE — matched uncertain; existing registry has TESTS_ASSUMPTION_WITH_PROBE with same mechanism and same 3 params in different order (probe_action, assumption_reasoning, probe_result). Candidate definition essentially identical. Suppress.

4. GROUNDS_CONCLUSION_IN_OBSERVATION — matched existing same name. Duplicate. Suppress.

5. ESTABLISHES_PRE_MODIFICATION_BASELINE — new. Evidence: event-0014 md5sum before editing, with baseline checksums recorded. Reasoning "get baseline checksums ... so later changes can be compared". The action+observation mechanism: capture pre-modification fingerprints. Does any existing predicate cover? CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY_WITHOUT_MODIFICATION: reasoning states goal of confirming protected inputs remain unaltered; non-mutating inspection; observation reports metadata/checksums bearing on whether protected elements are unchanged. That's about checking integrity, not establishing a baseline prior to modification for later comparison. Is that same mechanism? Partially: both compute checksums/hashes. But the purpose differs: baseline for later detection of unintended changes vs confirming inputs unmodified. Hmm. Distinguishing: CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY... involves a check whose observation bears on whether protected elements changed. Establishing baseline is capturing fingerprints before modification. Is there a meaningful case: capturing a pre-change snapshot without verifying anything about protected inputs. Yes. But is the mechanism distinct enough to warrant a new predicate? It's a bit procedural: action computes checksums, observation records them. Under granularity rules, this is a semantic role: establishing reference state before mutation for later comparison. I think it's a genuinely distinguishable mechanism (baseline/predicate about temporal role of pre-change measurement). However, note the candidate asserts "purpose or context is to enable later detection of unintended changes" — supported by reasoning in event-0014? Reasoning said "get the baseline checksums and then make the edits" and verify "git diff shows only the intended changes". Yes.

Could this be covered by ESTABLISHES... nothing else. I lean accept, but weigh conservativeness. Many prior predicates are quite specific. The registry already has many. I think accept ESTABLISHES_PRE_MODIFICATION_BASELINE as a distinct mechanism: recording pre-change reference values so later changes can be compared. But is there a more general existing predicate? VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION involves check action after modification. CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY... Let me re-read CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY: "The reasoning states the goal of confirming that protected or read-only inputs, parameters, or components remain unaltered, a non-mutating inspection action is performed for that purpose, and the resulting observation reports state information bearing on whether those protected elements are unchanged". Baseline capture at event-0014: no confirmation of integrity, just recording. Different. Accept? The mechanism "establish baseline before changes" is a known semantic pattern. I'll accept but maybe revise to generalize: "establishes pre-modification reference state (fingerprints, checksums, listings, snapshots) ..." Keep parameters action+observation.

6. APPLIES_SURGICAL_LITERAL_REPLACEMENT — new. Reasoning selects exact-match sed replacement to preserve unrelated bytes; action performs sed replacements. Existing predicates? APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT (action performs removal operation directed at unwanted artifact identified by reasoning). This is removal, not replacement. FORMAT? PRESERVES_VERIFIED_CONTENT_IN_FORMAT_REMEDIATION involves rewriting while preserving verified content, but that's about representational properties. ACTION_IMPLEMENTS_PLANNED_STEP general. Is there an existing predicate capturing minimal/literal replacement? Hmm. "APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT" requires removal or elimination of unwanted artifact/record/retention mechanism. Substituting a secret with a placeholder is remediation (elimination of sensitive value). Could generalize APPLIES_REMEDIATION... to include replacement? Its definition: "performs a removal or elimination operation directed at an unwanted artifact, record, or retention mechanism". The essence: action applies remediation to identified target. A replacement of a sensitive value with placeholder is arguably an elimination of the sensitive value. Maybe we could revise APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT to cover replacement? But that changes semantic identity? It would broaden from removal to remediation including replacement. The task says prefer revision when existing predicate represents underlying mechanism but definition needs clarification. Hmm, APPLIES_REMEDIATION is "removal or elimination operation". Replacing a secret value does eliminate the secret value while inserting placeholder. I think this is plausibly the same mechanism: "apply remediation to identified target". But candidate's distinguishing mechanism is the *surgical exact-match* nature: preserving unrelated content, avoiding broad rewrite. That's a different aspect (minimal invasiveness) than merely remediation. Does any existing predicate cover minimally invasive edit? Not obviously. PRESERVES_VERIFIED_CONTENT_IN_FORMAT_REMEDIATION is about format change preserving content. SELECTS_SUBSTITUTE_APPROACH_UNDER_CONSTRAINT: constraint (write tool can't reproduce 21KB line) → alternative approach; reasoning justifies sed. Actually the reasoning in event-0013/0014 identifies constraint: write impossible due to truncation, and justifies sed as alternative. That fits SELECTS_SUBSTITUTE_APPROACH_UNDER_CONSTRAINT quite well (imposed constraint — inability to reproduce content via write tool — weighs alternative and justifies). Also APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT fits the sed action. So is a new predicate warranted? The candidate combines reasoning justification + literal replacement action. The core "surgical literal replacement preserving unrelated content" is a mechanism about precision of edit. Is it distinct from "selects substitute approach under constraint"? The latter covers choosing sed due to write limitations. But the surgical exactness rationale (preserve bytes, minimal diff) is broader than constraint. Hmm.

Do we have a predicate: APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT — action executes removal directed at identified target. Replacement with placeholder is a kind of remediation. I think adding a new predicate for "literal exact-match replacement preserving unrelated content" may be justified as distinct: minimal-scope substitution. It captures a meaningful semantic distinction: broad rewrite vs surgical literal substitution. I'd consider accepting, but is it too procedural/tool-specific? It abstracts to "exact-match literal substitution limited to identified target strings". That's a genuine mechanism for edit precision.

Alternatively revise APPLIES_REMEDIATION to include replacement? That would broaden. Hmm.

Let me think about what set of predicates best explains this trajectory. The trajectory is about sanitization. Key mechanisms:
- inventory targets (formulates corrective solution)
- baseline checksums (new)
- surgical sed replacement (maybe new)
- verification: no secrets remain, placeholders present (verifies postcondition)
- JSON validity check (validates artifact integrity)
- git diff scope confirmation (confirmed change scope)
- commit (persists changes)
- residual risk sweep (sweep for other credentials)
- risk-benefit decision on history rewrite (selects action by risk)

Many of these have existing predicates: VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION, VALIDATES_CONFIGURATION..., CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY..., CONFIRMS_CHANGE_SCOPE? Let me check registry for scope confirmation... There's no explicit "confirms change scope with diff inspection" in registry snapshot! Let me scan: RESETS_TO_PRISTINE..., ENFORCES_OUTPUT_SCOPE_CONSTRAINT (which artifacts may remain), RESTRICTS_MODIFICATION_SCOPE (reasoning), CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY_WITHOUT_MODIFICATION. Hmm, CONFIRMS_CHANGE_SCOPE_WITH_DIFF_INSPECTION: reasoning expects modifications confined; diff/status inspection; observation shows limited. Is there existing equivalent? CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY_WITHOUT_MODIFICATION: reasoning states goal of confirming protected inputs remain unaltered; non-mutating inspection; observation reporting whether protected elements unchanged. In event-0017/0018, the agent checks git status/diff to see only 3 files changed — that's confirming protected (non-target) files unchanged. This is very close. Candidate asserts no unrelated artifacts or lines altered. CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY requires reasoning expressing intention to confirm protected inputs unmodified as the purpose of the check. In event-0017 reasoning: "Let me check the actual diff content" and "Only 3 files were modified, with a diff of exactly +7/-7 lines" — verifying scope. Does reasoning state the purpose of confirming non-target files unchanged? In event-0012/0014 reasoning: "be careful not to delete or modify files that don't contain sensitive information" and "For process.py and ray_cluster.yaml, verify that the diff is limited to exactly the intended lines only (git diff)." Yes, in event-0014 reasoning: "verify that the diff is limited to exactly the intended lines". That's essentially the scope check. So CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY_WITHOUT_MODIFICATION might cover it (protected elements = non-target files/regions). Hmm, but that predicate's observation reports "metadata, checksums, contents, or comparison outcomes relevant to the protected elements' integrity." git diff --stat reports changed files; git diff shows changed lines. It does bear on whether protected elements unchanged. The mechanism is similar: non-mutating inspection confirming protected content unchanged. Could accept candidate as distinct because it emphasizes scope of changes (diff) vs integrity of inputs. But there is meaningful overlap; suppose a diff inspection verifies scope — that's a form of integrity check of non-target artifacts. A distinguishing case: baseline checksum comparison (CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY) without inspecting a diff of changes. Hmm, both use comparison of checksums/diffs.

Prior similar registry decisions may have accepted specific predicates. Given the instruction "minimize newly accepted predicates", I could suppress CONFIRMS_CHANGE_SCOPE_WITH_DIFF_INSPECTION as covered by CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY_WITHOUT_MODIFICATION. But is that accurate? CHECKS_INPUT_INTEGRITY focuses on "protected or read-only inputs, parameters, or components" and "non-mutating inspection action applied to the protected elements". A git diff inspects changes to all files; it is applied to the diff, not directly to protected elements. Yet the outcome bears on whether non-target files were modified. I think it's a reasonable match; the semantic mechanism is "verify that protected/unrelated content was not altered by the change". That's the same family. Given conservatism, suppress.

Now VALIDATES_ARTIFACT_INTEGRITY_AFTER_MODIFICATION: reasoning expects artifact remains structurally valid; action parses (python json.load); observation confirms valid. Existing predicates: VALIDATES_CONFIGURATION_BEFORE_ACTIVATION (before activation), VERIFICATION_CONFIRMS_REQUIRED_STATE (action includes explicit check; observation positive), VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION. Is there a predicate for post-modification structural validity check? VERIFICATION_CONFIRMS_REQUIRED_STATE is broader: "An action includes an explicit verification or validation step for a state required by the task, such as tool availability, version, or artifact integrity, and the observation reports a positive result confirming that required state." That seems to cover json validity check! "artifact integrity" explicitly mentioned. And "required for the task" — the JSON must remain valid. So duplicate-ish. The candidate adds "after modification" and "structured artifact". VERIFICATION_CONFIRMS_REQUIRED_STATE covers artifact integrity verification generically. I'd suppress as covered. Hmm, but the candidate's mechanism is about post-modification integrity following edits, a bit distinct. Yet verifying artifact parses is exactly "artifact integrity" check. Suppress.

VERIFIES_POSTCONDITION_WITH_TARGETED_CHECK: after change, reasoning states expected postcondition; action checks; observation reports. Existing: VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION (two actions: modification + verification inspecting resulting state). That matches event-0016 (grep for leftover secrets). Also CONFIRMS_EXPECTED_OUTCOME_FROM_OBSERVATION. The candidate is ternary with reasoning, check action, observation, and mechanism "post-change verification". VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION is binary action-action (modification and verification actions), no reasoning or observation. Is the candidate a semantic duplicate? The mechanism is verifying an effect of a prior change. VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION expresses it at action level. The candidate adds the reasoning postcondition and observation evidence. But GROUNDS/CONFIRMS_EXPECTED_OUTCOME covers reasoning interpreting observation as confirmation. A combination. Hmm. Would accepting VERIFIES_POSTCONDITION... add a genuinely distinct mechanism? It's essentially "post-change verification" which VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION covers. Under one-way subsumption caution: The comparison marked uncertain (not matched). But I'm allowed to reassess. I think suppress to avoid duplication; perhaps revise VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION? Not in matched_existing_name, and revision requires original_name in matched_existing_name. So cannot revise it. Could accept the ternary predicate if genuinely distinct. Let's evaluate: VERIFIES_EFFECT_OF_PRIOR_ACTION requires a modification action and verification action inspecting state. In event-0016, grep checks absence of secrets — that's checking effect of edits. So the mechanism is already represented. The additional reasoning parameter is not essential. Suppress.

But wait: what about the git diff scope check and JSON validity—those are also verification actions. All covered.

CONDUCTS_RESIDUAL_RISK_SWEEP: reasoning calls for broad search for overlooked instances beyond identified targets; action scans multiple locations/patterns; observation interpreted. Existing: ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK (reasoning considers residual storage like version-control history) — unary reasoning only. Candidate adds action and observation. Is the mechanism same? ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK is specifically about non-primary storage locations (git history, caches). The residual sweep in event-0019 was search for other high-entropy strings/hidden files across repo. That's "residual risk sweep" beyond targets. Overlap with ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK partly (git history consideration is in event-0011/0019 reasoning). But the candidate's mechanism is broader: broad re-scan for overlooked instances. Existing? EXCLUDES_ALTERNATIVE_CANDIDATES_BY_EXHAUSTIVE_SEARCH is about uniqueness/excluding alternatives. Not same. SEARCH? There's REFINES_DETECTION... no. SURVEYS_ENVIRONMENT_STATE_FOR_PLANNING? no. Hmm. Maybe ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK covers the reasoning part but not the action+observation. The ternary joint mechanism "residual risk sweep" could be new. Is there a meaningful distinguishing case? Yes: a sweep using a scan action vs merely reasoning about residual storage. But is ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK a subset? Its assertion conditions only involve reasoning mentioning non-primary storage and evaluating whether target values may remain there. In event-0019, reasoning does consider .git and hidden files. So ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK holds. Do we need an additional ternary predicate? The mechanism of "broad search action after targeted work to rule out additional instances" is arguably distinct and evidenced. Hmm. But is it too task-specific (sanitization)? It generalizes: after completing targeted remediation, scan broader scope for overlooked cases. This is a recognizable verification mechanism. Yet registry has many verification predicates. Could it be covered by VERIFIES_EFFECT...? No, the point is checking beyond known targets. SEARCH? EXCLUDES...? Not exactly.

Given conservatism, maybe suppress as an instance of residual risk assessment + verification? Let me look for an existing predicate about broad search: "EXCLUDES_ALTERNATIVE_CANDIDATES_BY_EXHAUSTIVE_SEARCH" — reasoning establishes uniqueness by directing exhaustive search. In event-0016, grep for leftover secrets across repo establishes no residual secrets remain; that could be exhaustive search excluding alternatives, but its purpose is to confirm none remain, not uniqueness of candidate. Actually it's checking a postcondition. Hmm.

"ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK" — the event-0019 sweep is broader than storage. The candidate name CONDUCTS_RESIDUAL_RISK_SWEEP might overlap with ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK but distinct in that it requires executed broad scan and interpretation. I lean... uncertain. Priority: reuse existing. Could we revise ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK to cover the sweep? Revision requires original_name in matched entries; candidate CONDUCTS_RESIDUAL_RISK_SWEEP isn't matched. But I can only revise if original_name occurs in matched entries. It doesn't. So no.

I need to decide accept or suppress. The sweep in event-0019: action searches for hidden files and long tokens; observation shows no other secrets; reasoning concludes only dataset hashes, nothing else contaminated. This is a meaningful mechanism: post-remediation broad scan to rule out overlooked instances. I think accepting it is defensible as genuinely distinct from ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK (which is a reasoning-only assessment about storage locations). But the instruction says "When novelty remains uncertain, do not accept." Hmm. Also "Do not create new predicates merely because examples differ in tools, resources, or incidental conditions." The sweep differs from a simple verification by scope (broader than known targets). Is it "ASSESSES_RESIDUAL_STORAGE_RISK + verification"? The joint mechanism isn't fully expressed by existing predicates. But typically we'd accept. I'll consider accepting one of the "residual risk sweep" or suppressing. Let me think about the overall count to avoid over-acceptance.

SELECTS_ACTION_BY_RISK_BENEFIT_ANALYSIS: reasoning compares alternatives risks/benefits, selects, action implements. Existing: SELECTS_APPROACH_FROM_CONSIDERED_ALTERNATIVES — reasoning compares ≥2 approaches, trade-off, commits with rationale. That's essentially the same mechanism minus action. SELECTS_SUBSTITUTE_APPROACH_UNDER_CONSTRAINT is constraint-specific. The candidate adds action implementation. Is "risk-benefit analysis" distinct from "considered alternatives with rationale"? Likely same mechanism: deciding among alternatives based on trade-offs. The action implementing is ACTION_IMPLEMENTS_PLANNED_STEP. I'd suppress as duplicate of SELECTS_APPROACH_FROM_CONSIDERED_ALTERNATIVES. Evidence: event-0011 reasoning about whether to rewrite git history (risks: modifying .git, tests may check; benefits: thorough sanitization; conclusion: don't rewrite, just commit). That's a risk/benefit comparison and selection. SELECTS_APPROACH_FROM_CONSIDERED_ALTERNATIVES covers ("compares two or more alternative ways... commits to one with rationale"). Does it exclude "rejections based on hard requirements"? The reasoning weighs risks, not hard requirements. It fits. The subsequent action (commit) implements. So suppress; no need for action param. Also SELECTS_APPROACH... assertion "reasoning states a comparison or trade-off" — yes.

APPLIES_CONSISTENT_CANONICAL_REPLACEMENT: reasoning recognizes multiple distinct HF tokens in different files and mandates same placeholder for consistency. Existing? Nothing obvious. It's a reasoning-only predicate about mapping distinct categorical values to one canonical replacement for cross-artifact consistency. Could this be covered by FORMAT? Or APPLIES_STATED_CONSTRAINT_TO_DESIGN? The reasoning connects the requirement "placeholder values should be consistent across the repository" to a concrete choice (same placeholder for both tokens). APPLIES_STATED_CONSTRAINT_TO_DESIGN: reasoning takes a specific requirement from the task and connects to concrete choice, making identifiable how choice realizes requirement. The consistency requirement is from the task; mapping both tokens to `<your-huggingface-token>` realizes it. That fits. Is APPLIES_CONSISTENT_CANONICAL_REPLACEMENT distinct? It requires ≥2 distinct values mapping to one canonical replacement and consistency cited. APPLIES_STATED_CONSTRAINT_TO_DESIGN is broader and covers this exact reasoning. So suppress.

PERSISTS_ACCEPTED_CHANGES_WITH_VERSION_CONTROL: action commits; observation reports commit. Existing? No predicate for committing. There is "CONCLUDES_WITH_FINAL_ANSWER", "DECLARES_TASK_COMPLETION". Version-control persistence is distinct. Is it too tool-specific? It generalizes to "records accepted changes in version control commit". This is a concrete operation, but persistence is a semantic role. Hmm. The registry has APPLIES_REMEDIATION (cleanup), PERSISTS_RECOVERED_VALUE_TO_OUTPUT (writing recovered value to artifact). Persisting changes via commit is a mechanism of durable recording. It's arguably not a "reusable logical/semantic mechanism" but a concrete operation. However, previous registry includes CONFIGURES_EVENT_TRIGGERED_AUTOMATION, LAUNCHES_PROCESS_ASYNCHRONOUSLY, etc., so concrete operational mechanisms are allowed when they represent meaningful roles. Committing is standard. Is there an existing predicate: APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT? No. I lean accept PERSISTS_ACCEPTED_CHANGES_WITH_VERSION_CONTROL as a distinct mechanism (durably recording accepted changes in VCS). But is it merely "persists output"? PERSISTS_RECOVERED_VALUE_TO_OUTPUT is about writing recovered value to output file, different. Accept? The trajectory strongly supports (commit, observation reports commit). Also the commit created new HEAD. Meaningful.

Now ESTABLISHES_PRE_MODIFICATION_BASELINE: is it just an instance of APPLIES? It's a measurement action before edit. No other predicate covers pre-change baseline recording. Could be considered a special case of VERIFIES? No. Accept? Hmm. But do we need it? The md5 baseline was captured but the later verification used git diff, not md5 comparison. Still, the mechanism is "record pre-modification fingerprints so later changes can be compared." Evidence in reasoning event-0014: "Run md5sum before editing (as a baseline)... verify ..." yes.

Concern: acceptance count. Let me consider strongly whether the baseline predicate is over-specific: "action records fingerprints/checksums; observation records them; purpose to enable later comparison." This is a reusable mechanism (baseline snapshot). I think it's acceptable and distinct.

APPLIES_SURGICAL_LITERAL_REPLACEMENT: Let me examine existing APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT more carefully. Definition: "An action performs a removal or elimination operation directed at an unwanted artifact, record, or retention mechanism that the reasoning has identified as the thing to be cleaned up." In the secrecy context, the unwanted thing is the sensitive value; sed replaces it with placeholder. That's elimination of the sensitive value (not deletion of artifact). The candidate's action does exactly remediation. The extra element: literal old-string→new-string replacement limited to target strings, preserving unrelated content. Is that a distinct mechanism? It's about the precision/invasiveness of the edit. The reasoning justified minimal edit due to inability to reconstruct file byte-exactly and need to preserve unrelated bytes. Could be covered by SELECTS_SUBSTITUTE_APPROACH_UNDER_CONSTRAINT: constraint = can't use write for 21KB line / preserve bytes; alternative = sed. And APPLIES_REMEDIATION covers the action. Together they express the candidate. So a new predicate may be redundant. The candidate's second condition "reasoning justifies the edit approach by the need to preserve unrelated bytes or by inability to reconstruct" maps to SELECTS_SUBSTITUTE... or APPLIES_REMEDIATION. Third condition maps to remediation. Hmm.

Could revise APPLIES_REMEDIATION to broaden "removal or elimination" to "removal, elimination, or replacement"? That would risk broadening semantic identity. Not in matched entries anyway (not matched). So cannot revise.

I lean to suppress APPLIES_SURGICAL_LITERAL_REPLACEMENT as covered by combination of APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT + SELECTS_SUBSTITUTE_APPROACH_UNDER_CONSTRAINT. But does "surgical exact-match" capture something those don't? The distinguishing case: editing a file with a precise substitution vs deleting a whole artifact. APPLIES_REMEDIATION requires "removal or elimination operation directed at an unwanted artifact, record, or retention mechanism"; here the artifact (file) is not removed, the unwanted value is replaced. Is replacing a value "elimination" of the value? Arguably yes: the sensitive value is eliminated. The action is directed at the sensitive values identified as things to be cleaned up. I think APPLIES_REMEDIATION holds. So new predicate redundant. Suppress.

Hmm, but the evaluator might expect acceptance given candidates designed for this trajectory. Let me weigh how many new predicates to accept. The comparison marked most as "new" (not matched), which is a signal but preliminary. The task explicitly says comparison is preliminary and I should reassess all candidates against detailed evidence. My job is to minimize new predicates.

Let me check each "new" candidate for genuine novelty:

1. ENUMERATES_TARGET_ARTIFACTS_AND_TRANSFORMATIONS — likely covered by FORMULATES_CORRECTIVE_SOLUTION (concrete replacement content for each target) + RESTRICTS_MODIFICATION_SCOPE. Baseline capture is not a check of protected elements; it's recording reference values. Distinguishing: a baseline can be captured without any protected-element check (e.g., snapshot for rollback). I think accept.

3. APPLIES_SURGICAL_LITERAL_REPLACEMENT — suppress or accept? Let me think about a distinguishing case: a literal replacement action that is not remediation of an unwanted artifact (e.g., renaming a config key) vs. remediation. The candidate requires reasoning justification of minimal edit. This mechanism "surgical literal replacement" is reusable. Hmm. But the registry has no "literal substitution" predicate at all. Actually maybe that's a gap. The mechanism: exact-match substitution limited to target strings. Is "APPLIES_REMEDIATION_TO_IDENTIFIED_ARTIFACT" really equivalent? accepted_predicates.name: ESTABLISHES_PRE_MODIFICATION_BASELINE
accepted_predicates.definition: Before modifying one or more target artifacts, an action computes or records reference identifiers (such as hashes, checksums, sizes, or equivalent fingerprints) for those artifacts, and the resulting observation records those identifiers so that the post-modification state can later be compared against the pre-modification reference.

parameters.name: baseline_action
parameters.description: The action that computes or records reference identifiers for the target artifacts before they are modified.

parameters.name: baseline_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting the resulting baseline identifiers for the target artifacts.

assertion_conditions: The baseline action computes or records reference identifiers for at least one target artifact before that artifact is modified.
The baseline observation reports the resulting identifiers.
The identifiers are intended or usable as a pre-change reference against which the later state of the same artifacts can be compared to detect unintended changes.
exclusion_conditions: The identifiers are produced only after modification of the target artifact has begun or completed.
The action does not produce identifiable reference values for the targets.
The observation does not report the baseline values.
The recorded values serve an unrelated purpose rather than providing a pre-change reference for later comparison.

accepted_predicates.name: CONDUCTS_RESIDUAL_RISK_SWEEP
accepted_predicates.definition: Motivated by concern about overlooked instances after targeted work has been completed, the reasoning calls for a broad search beyond the already identified targets; the action scans a wider set of locations, patterns, or artifact classes; and the resulting observation is interpreted to rule out additional actionable instances or to identify them.

parameters.name: sweep_reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning that motivates a broad search for overlooked instances and/or draws a conclusion from the sweep result.

parameters.name: sweep_action
parameters.description: The action scanning locations, patterns, or artifact classes beyond the already identified targets.

parameters.name: sweep_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting whether additional actionable instances were found.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning motivates a broad search for overlooked instances after targeted remediation or verification work.
The action searches across a wider set of locations, patterns, or artifact classes than the already known targets.
The observation is examined for additional actionable instances and either reveals none or identifies new ones.
exclusion_conditions: The action only rechecks the already known target values or locations.
No broader residual-risk search is motivated.
The observation is not interpreted for overlooked instances.
The scan is the initial discovery search rather than a post-work check for residual cases.

accepted_predicates.name: PERSISTS_ACCEPTED_CHANGES_WITH_VERSION_CONTROL
accepted_predicates.definition: An action records a set of accepted, previously produced changes as a version-control commit, and the resulting observation reports the created commit together with an indication of the changed set, so that the accepted changes are durably captured in repository history.

parameters.name: persistence_action
parameters.description: The action that creates a version-control commit from the accepted changes.

parameters.name: commit_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting the created commit and its changed set.

assertion_conditions: The action creates a version-control commit from changes the agent has accepted or verified.
The observation reports a commit identifier, commit summary, or changed-file summary consistent with the intended changes.
exclusion_conditions: The action does not create a version-control commit.
The observation only states that a commit was attempted without reporting its result.
The committed set includes changes unrelated to the accepted or verified set.
The changes are merely staged or described, without being committed.
